I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation this year. I am 78, so I do not want to chase complicated or labor-heavy crops. In Quzhou County, winter wheat and summer maize fit the weather, the soil, and the irrigation conditions best, and I know how to manage them steadily. That matters more to me than taking extra market risk. I will plant improved winter wheat on the full area first, because it is reliable, easy for me to manage, and gives me grain and straw. After wheat harvest, I will follow with hybrid summer maize on the same land, because maize yields well here and matches the season tightly. I will use moderate fertilizer rather than pushing too hard, because at my age I care more about stable output, manageable fieldwork, and avoiding wasted input. I will plough before wheat to set up a good seedbed, then use rotary tillage after wheat for faster maize planting. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat here usually needs several waterings, while summer maize can use rainfall if the season is normal. I will spray only as needed but still keep basic disease, weed, and insect control, because I want the crop protected without making management too complicated.
